data.text/markdown:
Copenhagen 5-node FEATHER demo

This notebook intentionally keeps the example tiny:
  • Place: Copenhagen Municipality, Denmark
  • Amenity: hospital
  • Hospitals used: 1
  • Street nodes used by FEATHER: 5 connected nodes
  • theta_max = 2.5
  • eval_points = 2
  • order = 1
The goal is to make the difference between FEATHER and FEATHER_new easy to inspect.

data.text/markdown:
FEATHER settings

theta = [0.01 2.5 ]
order = 1 With eval_points = 2 and order = 1, each node receives only four FEATHER outputs:
  • cos_r1_theta0
  • cos_r1_theta1
  • sin_r1_theta0
  • sin_r1_theta1

Transition matrices

The first pair is ordinary FEATHER. The second pair is FEATHER_new using weight = 1 / edge_length.

data.text/markdown:
FEATHER visualization

Node labels contain the FEATHER output value being visualized.

FEATHER_new visualization

Same nodes, same hospital feature, same theta and order. Only the random-walk transition probabilities are changed by inverse edge-length weighting.

Difference: FEATHER_new - FEATHER

A value of zero means both methods produced the same value for that node. Non-zero values show exactly where weighting the edges changed the output.
